conviction_note: The bar is the company's own Q3 guide (non-GAAP RMB400-500M, set on 2026-08-25 when July and August data were already in hand), so the reported quarter should land inside it. The print turns on the first Q4 guide under the new CEO, the former chief risk officer, and on whether the buyback suspended in late June stays suspended. Company-guided credit deterioration and the proxies (PBOC consumer-credit contraction, banks cutting partner lists, the 2026-09-30 marketing rules) lean negative. Against that, the stock is down 52% since the last print, trades at about 2x annualised non-GAAP profit with RMB10.6B of cash against a $573M market cap, and is not crowded short. So p_up is 47, only slightly below 50, on an abs move of 16 (the implied 15.5, rounded up because a new guide period is coming and this name moved 14-19% on each of its last two prints). The scaled -0.96 and the finding sum of -1.2 agree in sign and size.

findings.finding: The reported quarter should land inside the company's own Q3 guide. Non-GAAP net income was guided to RMB400-500M (GAAP RMB360-460M) on 2026-08-25, when management already knew July volume was 15% below the Q2 average, had tightened risk further in August, and had seen August FPD3/FPD7 rise about 20% MoM and C-M2 rise about 25%. Lower originations also mean lower day-one provisions, which cushions profit. Consensus EPS of $0.46 is about the guide midpoint, and revenue consensus is $439.7M against Q2's $525.6M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline history is empty (the FPI 6-K path was blocked). Rebuilt from sources: on the Q2 print the ADS fell 18.9% from $11.53 to $9.35 on 2026-08-26 (https://www.webull.com/news/15899188369343488), driven by the weak Q3 guide rather than the quarter; after the Q1 2026 print a headline reported a 14.1% fall on a 'soft Q1 and cautious Q2 outlook' (https://longbridge.com/news/289004348). Both drops came from the outlook, not the reported line.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced: the guide is public and consensus sits on it. It is filed because a landing at or above the midpoint is what a market treating the guide as soft would not expect, and the 52% fall since the print shows the market doubting even the guide. If the market believed the guide, the ADS would not trade at about 2x annualised non-GAAP profit.
findings.independence: Shares one document family with finding 2 (the Q2 call). The guide ranges themselves are in the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/385508/qfin-holdings-announces-second-quarter-and-interim-2026-unaudited-financial-results-and-declares-semi-annual-dividend).

findings.finding: Credit is deteriorating on the company's own guidance. Management guided Q3 C-M2 'noticeably' up from 0.66% in Q2, said normalisation will take 'at least two to three quarters' because a nationwide crackdown on debt collectors left a severe shortage of collection capacity, said external funding costs rose about 25bp in July and August and should trend up through H2, and said no Q4 guide yet beyond 'extra cautious' planning for the rest of 2026. The first Q4 guide will be set under that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has driven the last two reactions: -18.9% on the Q3 guide (2026-08-26) and about -14% on the Q2 outlook after Q1. Each new guide disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down about 52% since the Q2 print with no new company disclosure. What is not priced is the size of the Q4 step. If the market expected Q4 near Q3, the ADS would trade nearer 4-5x earnings, not about 2x. The current price already implies a further leg down in profit, so a merely weak Q4 guide may not move it far. That is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Same call transcript as finding 1. Different-source corroboration of rising retail credit stress: Huxiu, 2026-11-03, reports retail NPL rates rising at several banks and one bank calling retail risk still rising (https://www.huxiu.com/article/4902676.html). PBOC data: household short-term loans fell RMB270B in October, and short-term consumer loan balances fell from RMB9.49T at end-2025 to RMB8.53T at end-September (https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202611143931361743.html; https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026111300032034). Both are proxies, not company numbers.

findings.finding: Peers guided Q3 worse than Qfin, and funding is concentrating on head platforms. FinVolution said its China loan volume fell about 50% in July against Qfin's -15%, and expects China volume to shrink significantly in Q3. Lexin expects Q3 originations to fall sharply QoQ and may post a net loss. Xiaoying gave no Q3 guide, citing significant uncertainty. Banks are cutting co-lending partner lists (Yilian Bank from 56 partners to 10, Fumin from 30 to 13, Lanhai from 28 to 13) while directing new business to large internet-linked and head listed platforms. No peer has reported Q3 2026 yet, so Qfin prints first.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found for this name on a relative-share line.
findings.why_not_priced: Qfin has sold off in line with the sector (no relative re-rating is visible in a -76% YTD tape). If the market priced Qfin as a share gainer in a shrinking pool, the drawdown since August would be visibly smaller than peers'. The Nov 1 bank-whitelist data post-dates Qfin's last call. This is a proxy: the article does not name Qfin, it names Lexin as kept by one bank.
findings.independence: Peer guidance comes from a different source, Beijing Business Daily via 10jqka, 2026-10-15 (https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20261015/c680748634.shtml). The Xiaoying Q2 call summary is on Xueqiu (https://www.xueqiu.com/S/XYF/406710494). The Nov 1 bank-whitelist article is a separate source.

findings.finding: Capital return is an open question at the print. The buyback was suspended in late June: Q2 repurchases were about 463k ADS at $15.19, against a lifetime plan average of $41.80. Cash and short-term investments are about RMB10.6B (around $1.5B, including restricted cash and deposits) against a $573M market cap. The 2030 convertibles raised about $677M of net proceeds. Management said it 'may need to build a larger financial buffer near term' but intends to keep a 'reasonable shareholder return policy'. Any resumption, or a convert repurchase at a discount, would land at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found within the sourced window. The company returned about RMB6.16B in buybacks and dividends in 2025 (https://finviz.com/news/338117/qfin-holdings-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-unaudited-financial-results-and-raises-semi-annual-dividend).
findings.why_not_priced: A market expecting a resumed buyback at a market cap under half of cash would not have let the ADS fall 52% since August. The stated buffer-building intent keeps the central size small. The upside tail is wide because a resumed program would be large relative to free float.
findings.independence: The suspension date and stance are from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/QFIN/Q22026). The Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-16 also says the buyback was suspended (https://finviz.com/news/423403/qfins-profit-floor-faces-its-first-test-as-credit-stress-and-funding-costs-bite).

findings.finding: This is the first print under a new CEO. Yan Zheng, chief risk officer since July 2020, replaced Haisheng Wu as CEO on 2026-09-21; Wu moved to the international business. A risk-officer CEO's first guide and provisioning stance are more likely to reset low (kitchen-sink) than to stretch.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CEO-transition print for this name was found.
findings.why_not_priced: The change is public, but its effect on the first guide is an inference, not a document. If the market expected a reset guide, the post-announcement tape would have absorbed it; the stock kept falling through October, which is consistent with partial pricing. Sized small because it is an inference.
findings.independence: The company release of 2026-09-20 is syndicated at https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-9-20-qfin-holdings-announces-changes-in-management-and-board-composition. That is the same document, so there is no independent corroboration of the reset thesis.

findings.finding: The 2026-09-30 online financial-product marketing rules restrict non-financial institutions and third-party platforms from marketing financial products and ban 'low threshold / instant / low rate' language. Commentary says they remove intermediate-page screening and raise customer-acquisition cost, which bears on Q4 volume and cost for a traffic-dependent platform.
findings.why_not_priced: The rule post-dates Qfin's last call, so its effect is not in the August guide. The Earnings Whispers preview notes that competitor exits have cut industry acquisition spending, which offsets it. This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed.
findings.independence: Huxiu (via search summary of https://www.tmtpost.com/7816684.html) also reports the September rule and the 24%/20% rate caps. This is a proxy.

findings.finding: Director Andrew Y. Yan sold about $4.9M of stock in two filings in late September 2026. Director Xiaohuan Chen bought about $3.3M between March and June 2026, at higher prices.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and public. It is filed for the panel; a director selling after the Q2 print and before the CEO change is weak information.

baseline_tension: No skew is available (null), so there is no directional statement to agree or disagree with. The findings lean slightly negative, in the direction of the -17% 20-day and -52% post-print run-down, so the negatives are partly priced, which is why they are sized small. The low short interest means no squeeze risk to the negatives, and no crowd to fuel a positive surprise either.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the reported-quarter finding lands inside the company's Q3 range, so it moved from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 3/7 plus the 52% post-print drift: the credit and guidance negative is partly priced by the run-down, so it moved from -1.5 to -1.0.
Rule 5 (proxies small): the peer/whitelist finding is a proxy that does not name the company, so it moved from +0.7 to +0.5. The marketing-rule finding moved from -0.7 to -0.5.
Rule 1 (inference about the reaction): the CEO-reset finding is an inference with no document, so it moved from -1.0 to -0.7.

Untrustworthy-history lesson: the reaction history was rebuilt from sourced prior prints (-18.9% on 2026-08-26, about -14% after Q1). That supports abs_move 16, and three straight guide disappointments moved p_up from 48 to 47, giving -0.96 scaled.

Rule 7: short interest was checked before the negatives (1.0 day to cover, about 1.6% of shares), so no crowded-short shrink was needed. The insider-sale and capital-return findings were left standing.
